1: # Protocol: MDPI submission package and guide
2: 
3: ## Objective
4: Collect and verify current official MDPI-wide and Genes-specific submission rules, download and organize official MDPI manuscript templates, compare whether Genes follows the same requirements as MDPI overall or has journal-specific differences, prepare a local submission-file checklist/package scaffold, and write a Chinese submission guide with practical cautions.
5: 
6: ## Inputs
7: - A-001: G-008 submission rules goal context — Keep this task inside digestion-stage submission-rule collection, not manuscript drafting.
8: - A-002: MDPI Instructions for Authors — Primary official source for MDPI-wide author instructions and required submission elements.
9: - A-003: MDPI manuscript templates page — Primary official source for downloading current MDPI manuscript templates.
10: - A-004: Genes Instructions for Authors — Primary official source for Genes-specific requirements and differences.
11: - A-005: Genes journal homepage — Use for Genes scope, article types, journal notices, APC/status links, and template links.
12: - A-006: MDPI submission system — Use for high-level submission workflow context only; do not log in.
13: - A-007: MDPI publication ethics and policies — Use for ethics, authorship, conflicts, data/code, AI/tool use, citations, and policy cautions.
14: - A-008: Existing magazine research outputs — Optional background from earlier Genes/MDPI research tasks; official sources remain authoritative.
15: - A-009: Broad web search for MDPI and Genes submission experience — Use to discover additional current resources, including official help pages, institutional guides, author experience posts, forum discussions, and template mirrors; classify authority level before using.
16: - A-010: Research community discussion sources — Use for practical experience and caution signals only, not as official rules.
17: - A-011: Institutional author and library guides — Use for checklist-style support and institutional cautions only, not as official rules.
18: 
19: ## Steps
20: 1. Plan the evidence-gathering strategy before collection. Define source tiers: official MDPI/Genes rule authority; official MDPI/SuSy/template support pages; institutional/library guides; author experience reports; public forum/community discussions; and prior local T004/T005/T008 journal research. State which questions each source tier can answer and which it cannot.
21: 2. Search and collect current sources broadly. The executor may use web search, official sites, template links, SuSy help pages, institutional guides, author experience posts, forums, and community discussions. Record access date, URL, page title, source tier, jurisdiction/context when relevant, and reliability caveat for every source.
22: 3. Verify current official source URLs and write a source map. Official MDPI and Genes pages remain the authority for rules; non-official sources may only provide practical caution, workflow interpretation, or experience signals. Record whether each official source is MDPI-wide, Genes-specific, template-specific, ethics/policy-specific, or submission-system-specific.
23: 4. Download current official MDPI manuscript templates and any official linked template package needed for Word/LaTeX submission. Save downloaded files under the task artifact archive/document area with original filenames when possible, and write a checksum/source table for each downloaded file. If a non-official mirror is useful for comparison, record it separately and do not use it as the template authority.
24: 5. Extract and summarize MDPI-wide submission requirements: article types, manuscript structure, formatting expectations, references/citations, figures/tables, supplementary files, cover letter or suggested reviewers if applicable, data/code availability, ethics statements, conflict of interest, funding, acknowledgments, author contribution, AI/tool-use disclosure, and submission-system steps.
25: 6. Extract and summarize Genes-specific requirements and compare them against MDPI-wide rules. Produce an explicit same/different table: what is identical MDPI-wide, what is Genes-specific, what is unclear, and what must be checked immediately before actual submission.
26: 7. Synthesize practical experience signals from non-official sources. Separate them from rules and label them as author experience, forum discussion, institutional checklist, or cautionary anecdote. Use them to enrich submission注意点, but do not present them as official requirements.
27: 8. Build a local submission package scaffold and file checklist for a Genes/MDPI submission. Include expected manuscript file, cover letter if needed, figures, tables, supplementary materials, graphical abstract only if required or useful, data/code availability text, author declarations, ethics/consent statements, conflict/funding statements, and template files.
28: 9. Write a Chinese practical submission guide. It should explain what files to prepare, how to use the MDPI template, what to check before upload, what common issues can delay submission, which rules are MDPI-wide versus Genes-specific, which items come from community experience, and which parts require final human verification.
29: 10. Write a concise submission caution note focused on risk points: formatting overfit, missing statements, data/code availability, image/table quality, reference style, ethics/consent, authorship/affiliation consistency, AI-use disclosure, plagiarism/self-plagiarism, cover-letter tone, scope fit, APC/payment/admin issues, submission-system metadata, and changes in official rules.
30: 11. Produce a final HTML/Markdown dashboard that links all downloaded templates, source snapshots/tables, checklist, same/different comparison, package scaffold, practical experience source map, caution note, and Chinese submission guide.
31: 
32: ## Constraints

34: - The task should collect rules and prepare a package scaffold only. Do not draft the manuscript, invent author information, or fabricate declarations.
35: - Do not log into MDPI SuSy or use credentials in this task.
36: - Do not store API keys, passwords, submission account data, or private author information.
37: - Because submission rules and templates can change, record access date and exact source URL for every rule, downloaded template, non-official guide, and community source.
38: - If the official template download fails, record the failure, source URL, and retry path; do not substitute an unofficial template without explicit caveat.
39: - The guide must clearly distinguish MDPI-wide requirements from Genes-specific requirements.
40: - If Genes and MDPI-wide requirements appear consistent, state the evidence and still list the Genes page as the immediate pre-submission check source.
41: - Non-official sources must be clearly labeled as experience/context/caution, not requirements. Conflicts between non-official sources and official MDPI/Genes pages must be resolved in favor of official pages.

# Protocol: MDPI submission package and guide

## Objective
Collect and verify current official MDPI-wide and Genes-specific submission rules, download and organize official MDPI manuscript templates, compare whether Genes follows the same requirements as MDPI overall or has journal-specific differences, prepare a local submission-file checklist/package scaffold, and write a Chinese submission guide with practical cautions.

## Inputs
- A-001: G-008 submission rules goal context — Keep this task inside digestion-stage submission-rule collection, not manuscript drafting.
- A-002: MDPI Instructions for Authors — Primary official source for MDPI-wide author instructions and required submission elements.
- A-003: MDPI manuscript templates page — Primary official source for downloading current MDPI manuscript templates.
- A-004: Genes Instructions for Authors — Primary official source for Genes-specific requirements and differences.
- A-005: Genes journal homepage — Use for Genes scope, article types, journal notices, APC/status links, and template links.
- A-006: MDPI submission system — Use for high-level submission workflow context only; do not log in.
- A-007: MDPI publication ethics and policies — Use for ethics, authorship, conflicts, data/code, AI/tool use, citations, and policy cautions.
- A-008: Existing magazine research outputs — Optional background from earlier Genes/MDPI research tasks; official sources remain authoritative.
- A-009: Broad web search for MDPI and Genes submission experience — Use to discover additional current resources, including official help pages, institutional guides, author experience posts, forum discussions, and template mirrors; classify authority level before using.
- A-010: Research community discussion sources — Use for practical experience and caution signals only, not as official rules.
- A-011: Institutional author and library guides — Use for checklist-style support and institutional cautions only, not as official rules.

## Steps
1. Plan the evidence-gathering strategy before collection. Define source tiers: official MDPI/Genes rule authority; official MDPI/SuSy/template support pages; institutional/library guides; author experience reports; public forum/community discussions; and prior local T004/T005/T008 journal research. State which questions each source tier can answer and which it cannot.
2. Search and collect current sources broadly. The executor may use web search, official sites, template links, SuSy help pages, institutional guides, author experience posts, forums, and community discussions. Record access date, URL, page title, source tier, jurisdiction/context when relevant, and reliability caveat for every source.
3. Verify current official source URLs and write a source map. Official MDPI and Genes pages remain the authority for rules; non-official sources may only provide practical caution, workflow interpretation, or experience signals. Record whether each official source is MDPI-wide, Genes-specific, template-specific, ethics/policy-specific, or submission-system-specific.
4. Download current official MDPI manuscript templates and any official linked template package needed for Word/LaTeX submission. Save downloaded files under the task artifact archive/document area with original filenames when possible, and write a checksum/source table for each downloaded file. If a non-official mirror is useful for comparison, record it separately and do not use it as the template authority.
5. Extract and summarize MDPI-wide submission requirements: article types, manuscript structure, formatting expectations, references/citations, figures/tables, supplementary files, cover letter or suggested reviewers if applicable, data/code availability, ethics statements, conflict of interest, funding, acknowledgments, author contribution, AI/tool-use disclosure, and submission-system steps.
6. Extract and summarize Genes-specific requirements and compare them against MDPI-wide rules. Produce an explicit same/different table: what is identical MDPI-wide, what is Genes-specific, what is unclear, and what must be checked immediately before actual submission.
7. Synthesize practical experience signals from non-official sources. Separate them from rules and label them as author experience, forum discussion, institutional checklist, or cautionary anecdote. Use them to enrich submission注意点, but do not present them as official requirements.
8. Build a local submission package scaffold and file checklist for a Genes/MDPI submission. Include expected manuscript file, cover letter if needed, figures, tables, supplementary materials, graphical abstract only if required or useful, data/code availability text, author declarations, ethics/consent statements, conflict/funding statements, and template files.
9. Write a Chinese practical submission guide. It should explain what files to prepare, how to use the MDPI template, what to check before upload, what common issues can delay submission, which rules are MDPI-wide versus Genes-specific, which items come from community experience, and which parts require final human verification.
10. Write a concise submission caution note focused on risk points: formatting overfit, missing statements, data/code availability, image/table quality, reference style, ethics/consent, authorship/affiliation consistency, AI-use disclosure, plagiarism/self-plagiarism, cover-letter tone, scope fit, APC/payment/admin issues, submission-system metadata, and changes in official rules.
11. Produce a final HTML/Markdown dashboard that links all downloaded templates, source snapshots/tables, checklist, same/different comparison, package scaffold, practical experience source map, caution note, and Chinese submission guide.

## Constraints
- Use official MDPI/Genes sources as the authority for rules. Do not let third-party instructions override official pages, but do collect and cite third-party/institutional/forum experience as practical context when useful.
- The task should collect rules and prepare a package scaffold only. Do not draft the manuscript, invent author information, or fabricate declarations.

- Do not store API keys, passwords, submission account data, or private author information.

1: # Protocol: MDPI cross-journal affiliation and PUMCH publication landscape
2: 
3: ## Objective
4: 
5: Study MDPI journals beyond Genes to determine where China, hospital, bioinformatics/computational, and PUMCH/Beijing Union Medical College Hospital related-unit papers have recently appeared. The goal is to map published-paper presence and monthly trends across MDPI journals, not to design a PxFquery manuscript.
6: 
7: ## Inputs
8: 
9: - A-001: T004 Genes metadata and timing corpus — Reference corpus shape, crawl-output field names, publication-date fields, and timing analysis style.
10: - A-002: T006 Genes affiliation timing analysis ready table — Reusable affiliation, country, hospital, bioinformatics/computational, and C/H/B operational definitions.
11: - A-003: T006 PUMCH related publication records — Reusable PUMCH containing-match implementation, broader PUMC/CAMS separation pattern, and example record format.
12: - A-004: T008 MDPI cross-journal affiliation analysis-ready corpus — Reopened-task internal corpus for supplementary PUMCH month-by-journal heatmap, Chinese hospital counts, PUMCH relative position, and hospital ranking/count correlation.
13: 
14: ## Steps
15: 
16: 1. Write a data-source feasibility note before crawling. Compare MDPI pages, Crossref, PubMed/Europe PMC, and Google Scholar for reproducibility, affiliation coverage, monthly date coverage, rate limits, and journal coverage. Decide whether to start with all MDPI journals or a biologically relevant MDPI subset, and document the reason.
17: 2. Build an MDPI journal universe table with journal title, short name, ISSN/eISSN when available, MDPI URL, subject area, active status, and whether it is relevant to genetics, molecular biology, medicine, oncology, bioinformatics, systems biology, omics, or clinical research.
18: 3. Build a metadata corpus for the chosen MDPI journals over the recent three-year window. At minimum capture journal, DOI, title, publication date, article type, abstract, authors when available, URL, issue/volume, and source. Do not download full PDFs during the initial corpus build.
19: 4. Enrich affiliation text using a transparent source hierarchy: MDPI article page first when accessible, PubMed/Europe PMC second for indexed records, Crossref third when useful, and temporary PDF first-page extraction only for selected missing records. Record source, confidence, and missingness.
20: 5. Define and apply reusable flags: China affiliation, hospital/medical center affiliation, China + hospital combination, bioinformatics/computational-like content, China + hospital + bioinformatics/computational combination, PUMCH containing match, PUMCH first-unit containing match, broader PUMC/CAMS related match, and broader PUMC/CAMS first-unit match.
21: 6. Analyze monthly and quarterly trends by journal and overall. Include all seven China/hospital/bioinformatics combinations where practical: C, H, B, C+H, C+B, H+B, and C+H+B. Separately analyze PUMCH-containing and broader PUMC/CAMS-related records without requiring bioinformatics unless explicitly stated.
22: 7. Create concrete paper lists. For each important journal-pattern-month combination, list titles, dates, first-author first affiliation, matched affiliation text, article type, topic/method summary, DOI, and MDPI URL. This must be readable without opening a spreadsheet.
23: 8. Summarize MDPI publisher-level policy/news context only as context. Do not let policy discussion replace published-paper evidence.
24: 9. Produce a Chinese HTML dashboard with visualizations: journal-by-month heatmaps, top journal ranking, C/H/B combination trend panels, PUMCH monthly trend panels, concrete paper cards, and journal filters. Also produce Markdown and Excel/CSV support tables.
25: 10. Add a supplementary PUMCH-focused analysis: build PUMCH month-by-MDPI-journal count matrices for any-affiliation and first-unit matches, generate a direct heatmap visualization, and list concrete PUMCH papers supporting the counts.
26: 11. Add a supplementary China-hospital analysis: build an auditable hospital alias/ranking table from web-searched China hospital ranking evidence, count MDPI papers by hospital from A-004 affiliation text, locate PUMCH's relative position, and visualize the ecological association between external hospital rank and MDPI publication count.
27: 
28: ## Constraints
29: 
30: - This is not a PxFquery design or manuscript-planning task. Avoid wording that recommends project changes unless a later task asks for it.
31: - Published-paper data cannot estimate rejection rate, desk-reject rate, or acceptance probability.
32: - Google Scholar results are not a stable primary statistical source. Use them only for discovery/cross-check unless the task records a reason no better source works.
33: - Do not crawl or persist all PDFs up front. Use PDF extraction only as a targeted fallback for affiliation or selected paper-level detail.
34: - PUMCH must be treated as a containing-text match, especially `first_author_first_affiliation` containing `Peking Union Medical College Hospital`, not as exact affiliation equality. Broader CAMS/PUMC related units must be reported separately.
35: - The HTML report must be readable and visual, not only tables.
36: - API keys and credentials are runtime-only and must not be written to outputs.
37: - Write all outputs under T008. Do not modify T004/T006 source artifacts.
38: - Supplementary analysis must not overwrite the original T008 v20260618 outputs; write new supplementary outputs with explicit `supplement_` names or new workbook sheets/files.
39: - Hospital-name matching must be transparent and auditable. Use explicit aliases and preserve a match-method column.
40: - External hospital ranking evidence must be cited in the supplementary report. If the latest ranking uses tiers rather than strict numeric rank, document the fallback or mapping decision.
41: - The ranking-count correlation must be described as an ecological association only, not causal evidence of MDPI preference or editorial preference.
42: 
43: ## Deliverables
44: 
45: - Data-source feasibility report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_cross_journal_data_source_feasibility_v20260618.md`
46: - MDPI journal universe table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_journal_universe_v20260618.xlsx`
47: - Three-year MDPI metadata corpus: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_metadata_corpus_v20260618.csv.gz`
48: - Affiliation enrichment status and parsed affiliation table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_affiliation_enrichment_v20260618.xlsx`
49: - Monthly trend tables for C/H/B combinations and PUMCH/PUMC/CAMS patterns: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_monthly_trends_v20260618.xlsx`
50: - Concrete paper lists workbook: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_pattern_paper_lists_v20260618.xlsx`
51: - Main Chinese HTML dashboard: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_cross_journal_affiliation_landscape_dashboard_v20260618.html`
52: - Main Chinese Markdown report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_cross_journal_affiliation_landscape_report_v20260618.md`

54: - Supplementary China hospital alias and ranking table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/china_hospital_alias_rank_table_supplement_v20260618.xlsx`
55: - Supplementary China hospital MDPI count table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_china_hospital_publication_counts_supplement_v20260618.xlsx`
56: - Supplementary hospital rank correlation table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_hospital_rank_correlation_supplement_v20260618.xlsx`

59: - Supplementary Chinese Markdown report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_pumch_hospital_rank_supplement_report_v20260618.md`
60: - Supplementary Chinese HTML dashboard section/report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_pumch_hospital_rank_supplement_dashboard_v20260618.html`
61: - Completion report: `{taskPath}/5_report/completion.md`
62: 
63: ## Failure Stop
64: 
65: - No reproducible metadata source can produce journal, DOI/title, and monthly publication dates for a meaningful MDPI corpus.

70: 
71: ## Notes
72:

74:

76: 2. For each relevant journal, how do monthly counts change over time?
77: 3. Which journals contain papers whose first-author first affiliation or any affiliation includes PUMCH / Peking Union Medical College Hospital / 北京协和医院?
78: 4. Which journals contain broader PUMC/CAMS/中国医学科学院/北京协和医学院 related units, and how should those be separated from PUMCH hospital itself?
79: 5. What concrete papers exist for each pattern, and what are those papers doing scientifically?
80: 6. Which data source strategy is reproducible enough: MDPI article/search pages, Crossref, PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar, or a hybrid?

# Protocol: MDPI cross-journal affiliation and PUMCH publication landscape

## Objective

Study MDPI journals beyond Genes to determine where China, hospital, bioinformatics/computational, and PUMCH/Beijing Union Medical College Hospital related-unit papers have recently appeared. The goal is to map published-paper presence and monthly trends across MDPI journals, not to design a PxFquery manuscript.

## Inputs

- A-001: T004 Genes metadata and timing corpus — Reference corpus shape, crawl-output field names, publication-date fields, and timing analysis style.
- A-002: T006 Genes affiliation timing analysis ready table — Reusable affiliation, country, hospital, bioinformatics/computational, and C/H/B operational definitions.
- A-003: T006 PUMCH related publication records — Reusable PUMCH containing-match implementation, broader PUMC/CAMS separation pattern, and example record format.
- A-004: T008 MDPI cross-journal affiliation analysis-ready corpus — Reopened-task internal corpus for supplementary PUMCH month-by-journal heatmap, Chinese hospital counts, PUMCH relative position, and hospital ranking/count correlation.

## Steps

1. Write a data-source feasibility note before crawling. Compare MDPI pages, Crossref, PubMed/Europe PMC, and Google Scholar for reproducibility, affiliation coverage, monthly date coverage, rate limits, and journal coverage. Decide whether to start with all MDPI journals or a biologically relevant MDPI subset, and document the reason.
2. Build an MDPI journal universe table with journal title, short name, ISSN/eISSN when available, MDPI URL, subject area, active status, and whether it is relevant to genetics, molecular biology, medicine, oncology, bioinformatics, systems biology, omics, or clinical research.
3. Build a metadata corpus for the chosen MDPI journals over the recent three-year window. At minimum capture journal, DOI, title, publication date, article type, abstract, authors when available, URL, issue/volume, and source. Do not download full PDFs during the initial corpus build.
4. Enrich affiliation text using a transparent source hierarchy: MDPI article page first when accessible, PubMed/Europe PMC second for indexed records, Crossref third when useful, and temporary PDF first-page extraction only for selected missing records. Record source, confidence, and missingness.
5. Define and apply reusable flags: China affiliation, hospital/medical center affiliation, China + hospital combination, bioinformatics/computational-like content, China + hospital + bioinformatics/computational combination, PUMCH containing match, PUMCH first-unit containing match, broader PUMC/CAMS related match, and broader PUMC/CAMS first-unit match.
6. Analyze monthly and quarterly trends by journal and overall. Include all seven China/hospital/bioinformatics combinations where practical: C, H, B, C+H, C+B, H+B, and C+H+B. Separately analyze PUMCH-containing and broader PUMC/CAMS-related records without requiring bioinformatics unless explicitly stated.
7. Create concrete paper lists. For each important journal-pattern-month combination, list titles, dates, first-author first affiliation, matched affiliation text, article type, topic/method summary, DOI, and MDPI URL. This must be readable without opening a spreadsheet.
8. Summarize MDPI publisher-level policy/news context only as context. Do not let policy discussion replace published-paper evidence.
9. Produce a Chinese HTML dashboard with visualizations: journal-by-month heatmaps, top journal ranking, C/H/B combination trend panels, PUMCH monthly trend panels, concrete paper cards, and journal filters. Also produce Markdown and Excel/CSV support tables.
10. Add a supplementary PUMCH-focused analysis: build PUMCH month-by-MDPI-journal count matrices for any-affiliation and first-unit matches, generate a direct heatmap visualization, and list concrete PUMCH papers supporting the counts.
11. Add a supplementary China-hospital analysis: build an auditable hospital alias/ranking table from web-searched China hospital ranking evidence, count MDPI papers by hospital from A-004 affiliation text, locate PUMCH's relative position, and visualize the ecological association between external hospital rank and MDPI publication count.

## Constraints

- This is not a PxFquery design or manuscript-planning task. Avoid wording that recommends project changes unless a later task asks for it.
- Published-paper data cannot estimate rejection rate, desk-reject rate, or acceptance probability.
- Google Scholar results are not a stable primary statistical source. Use them only for discovery/cross-check unless the task records a reason no better source works.
- Do not crawl or persist all PDFs up front. Use PDF extraction only as a targeted fallback for affiliation or selected paper-level detail.
- PUMCH must be treated as a containing-text match, especially `first_author_first_affiliation` containing `Peking Union Medical College Hospital`, not as exact affiliation equality. Broader CAMS/PUMC related units must be reported separately.
- The HTML report must be readable and visual, not only tables.
- API keys and credentials are runtime-only and must not be written to outputs.
- Write all outputs under T008. Do not modify T004/T006 source artifacts.
- Supplementary analysis must not overwrite the original T008 v20260618 outputs; write new supplementary outputs with explicit `supplement_` names or new workbook sheets/files.
- Hospital-name matching must be transparent and auditable. Use explicit aliases and preserve a match-method column.
- External hospital ranking evidence must be cited in the supplementary report. If the latest ranking uses tiers rather than strict numeric rank, document the fallback or mapping decision.
- The ranking-count correlation must be described as an ecological association only, not causal evidence of MDPI preference or editorial preference.

## Deliverables

- Data-source feasibility report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_cross_journal_data_source_feasibility_v20260618.md`
- MDPI journal universe table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_journal_universe_v20260618.xlsx`
- Three-year MDPI metadata corpus: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_metadata_corpus_v20260618.csv.gz`
- Affiliation enrichment status and parsed affiliation table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_affiliation_enrichment_v20260618.xlsx`
- Monthly trend tables for C/H/B combinations and PUMCH/PUMC/CAMS patterns: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_monthly_trends_v20260618.xlsx`
- Concrete paper lists workbook: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_cross_journal_pattern_paper_lists_v20260618.xlsx`
- Main Chinese HTML dashboard: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_cross_journal_affiliation_landscape_dashboard_v20260618.html`
- Main Chinese Markdown report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_cross_journal_affiliation_landscape_report_v20260618.md`
- Supplementary PUMCH month-by-journal table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_pumch_month_journal_matrix_supplement_v20260618.xlsx`
- Supplementary China hospital alias and ranking table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/china_hospital_alias_rank_table_supplement_v20260618.xlsx`
- Supplementary China hospital MDPI count table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_china_hospital_publication_counts_supplement_v20260618.xlsx`
- Supplementary hospital rank correlation table: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/5_table/mdpi_hospital_rank_correlation_supplement_v20260618.xlsx`
- Supplementary PUMCH monthly heatmap image: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/4_picture/mdpi_pumch_month_journal_heatmap_supplement_v20260618.png`
- Supplementary hospital rank-count scatter image: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/4_picture/mdpi_hospital_rank_count_correlation_supplement_v20260618.png`
- Supplementary Chinese Markdown report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_pumch_hospital_rank_supplement_report_v20260618.md`
- Supplementary Chinese HTML dashboard section/report: `{taskPath}/4_artifact/2_persist/mdpi_pumch_hospital_rank_supplement_dashboard_v20260618.html`
- Completion report: `{taskPath}/5_report/completion.md`

## Failure Stop

- No reproducible metadata source can produce journal, DOI/title, and monthly publication dates for a meaningful MDPI corpus.
- Affiliation coverage is too low to support the affiliation questions and no missingness-aware fallback is acceptable.
- The task would require using Google Scholar as the sole source for systematic monthly counts.
- The work drifts into PxFquery design instead of journal/publisher fact-finding.
- The supplementary hospital ranking source cannot be made auditable enough for even an explicitly caveated ecological correlation analysis.

## Notes

Core questions:

1. Across MDPI journals, which journals publish China + hospital + bioinformatics/computational papers in the recent three-year window?
2. For each relevant journal, how do monthly counts change over time?
3. Which journals contain papers whose first-author first affiliation or any affiliation includes PUMCH / Peking Union Medical College Hospital / 北京协和医院?
4. Which journals contain broader PUMC/CAMS/中国医学科学院/北京协和医学院 related units, and how should those be separated from PUMCH hospital itself?
5. What concrete papers exist for each pattern, and what are those papers doing scientifically?
6. Which data source strategy is reproducible enough: MDPI article/search pages, Crossref, PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar, or a hybrid?

External sources to evaluate during Step 1 include MDPI journal index and journal-specific article listing/search pages, Crossref Works API, PubMed / NCBI E-utilities, Europe PMC, Google Scholar as discovery or sanity-check only, and official MDPI policy and journal information pages for publisher-level context.

# MDPI Reference List and Citations Style Guide

MDPI recommends that references be prepared with a bibliography software package such as EndNote or ReferenceManager, if a manuscript is prepared using MS Word. Alternatively, the free software [Zotero](http://www.zotero.org/) can be used. Zotero is a tool that helps you collect, organize, and cite your references. For LaTeX users, we strongly recommend preparing references using BibTeX. If references are prepared manually, the authors should check them for completeness and correctness. For this purpose, authors may use [Web of Science](http://apps.isiknowledge.com/)![external_link](https://www.mdpi.com/img/design/www-link.png), [PubMed/MEDLINE](http://www.pubmed.com/)![external_link](https://www.mdpi.com/img/design/www-link.png), or [Google Scholar](http://scholar.google.com/)![external_link](https://www.mdpi.com/img/design/www-link.png).

EndNote Users: Please download the MDPI.ens reference style file from the EndNote website at [http://endnote.com/downloads/style/mdpi](http://endnote.com/downloads/style/mdpi)![external-link](https://www.mdpi.com/img/design/www-link.png).
